PLAN: spigot 0.1.1 — simplification pass

Source: PLAN.md

The 0.1.0 build plan (M0–M7, 487 lines) is archived: git show v0.1.0:PLAN.md. DECISIONS.md holds the record of what was decided and why; this file holds only what is still to do.

This release changes no user-facing behaviour. It removes code that a review on 2026-10-16 found to be carrying weight nothing needs: compatibility shims with no compatibility gain, machinery for states the code cannot reach, two mechanisms for one rule, and prose that lives in two places. Where a simplification makes spigot slightly more permissive, the plan says so and DECISIONS.md gets an entry.

1. Ground rules

  • Test-first. Each step names the test change before the code change. Where a behaviour is removed, its test is removed in the same commit, never left failing.
  • Behaviour is the spec. The e2e and integration tests (test-client.R, test-push.R, test-trigger.R, test-page.R, test-mount.R) must pass unchanged except where a step below says otherwise. A step that needs a test rewritten beyond what is listed here has found a behaviour change; stop and record it in DECISIONS.md before continuing.
  • .Rd files are generated by devtools::document(), never edited by hand.
  • One commit per milestone, suite green with Chrome (skip_if_no_chrome() must not skip locally) before committing. CI (4 cells, including shiny 1.11.0) green before M13.
  • Line references below are to the 0.1.0 sources (56cf110). They drift as earlier milestones land; the function names are the stable anchor.

2. Verification, every milestone

devtools::document()
devtools::test()                        # Chrome installed; no e2e skips
rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = "--no-manual")

Expectation count at 0.1.0: 965. It goes down in M8–M10 (tests for removed behaviour) and should otherwise be flat. A rise means a step added a test that this plan did not call for; that is fine, but note it in the commit message.

3. Milestones

M8: R internals

Four independent cleanups in R/, one commit. None changes a message that a test matches, except where noted.

8.1 One scalar check. is_string() lives in R/page.R:113; eight other sites spell it out.

  1. Test: new test-utils.R with cases for is_string() and is_flag() (neither has a unit test today; test-helpers.R tests the test helpers, not R/utils.R). is_string(): accepts a length-1 non-NA character; rejects NA_character_, character(0), c("a","b"), 1.
  2. Move is_string() to R/utils.R. Use it at R/api.R:24, R/examples.R:41, R/mount.R:7 (check_prefix), R/session.R:11 (is_token), :98 (check_event), :288 (spigot_trigger name), :331 (resolve_trigger).
  3. Use is_flag() for the filter return check at R/session.R:202.
  4. spigot_emit() at R/session.R:167 checks is.function(session$sendCustomMessage); spigot_trigger() uses is_session(). Both use is_session(). The error text (“session must be a Shiny session or NULL.”) stays; test-push.R:45 matches on “session”.

8.2 Checks for unreachable states.

  1. mount_app() (R/mount.R:74-81): delete the shiny.appobj and httpHandler checks. It is internal and only ever receives shiny::shinyApp()’s result. (Its message also claimed shiny >= 1.14.0 while DESCRIPTION says 1.11.0.) Delete the test test-mount.R:157 “mount_app() only accepts a shiny.appobj with an httpHandler”.
  2. register_session() (R/session.R:19-21): delete the idempotency early return. Only wrap_server() calls it, once per session. Delete test-session.R:15 “registering twice is idempotent” and the callbacks() counter in helper-session.R (that test is its only reader).
  3. spigot_app() (R/app.R:75-76): delete the two missing() checks. R’s own “argument”pages” is missing, with no default” is enough. No test matches them.

8.3 spigot_broadcast(). test-push.R:62-235 is the spec and does not change. except = and filter = stay; only the implementation shrinks.

  1. Add live_sessions() next to lookup_session(): as.list(.registry, all.names = TRUE), prune any whose isClosed() is TRUE, return the rest unnamed.
  2. Rewrite the body as three Filter()/vapply() passes over live_sessions(): drop except (identity after root_session()), apply filter (every session before any send, is_flag() on each result, as now), then send with the tryCatch that prunes on failure. Return invisible(sum(sent)).
  3. prune_session() is a one-line alias of unregister_session(); inline it or keep it, but not both names for one thing. test-push.R:235 “prune_session() removes only that session” tests the behaviour, so keep whichever name it calls.

8.4 Small things.

  1. page_router() (R/page.R:293): delete the /reactlog special case and the test test-page.R:220. A spigot app answers /reactlog with its own 404. DECISIONS entry: reactlog is a development tool; a user who needs it under spigot can add a page or open an issue.
  2. strsplit_first() (R/page.R:242): sub("^/([^/]*).*$", "\\1", path).
  3. base_href() (R/page.R:247): lengths(strsplit(path, "/", fixed = TRUE)) - 2L is the depth ("/" gives -1, "/docs/intro" gives 1). The existing tests at test-page.R:276-310 cover every depth.
  4. spigot_serializer() (R/api.R:36): pass spigot_json itself, not function(val) spigot_json(val).

M9: Mount handler without path restore

Why. spigot_mount_handler() (R/mount.R:36-61) restores PATH_INFO and SCRIPT_NAME after plumber answers: on.exit for sync results, promises::finally() for async, with an async flag to pick one. Shiny’s routeHandler does the same because a routed handler may return NULL and let the next handler see the request. shiny:::joinHandlers (checked, 1.14.0) only moves to the next handler on NULL. After the rewrite, spigot’s handler never returns NULL: the guard, pr$call() and mount_failure() all return a response. Nothing reads the request afterwards.

  1. Tests, test-mount.R:
    • :32 “the prefix moves from PATH_INFO to SCRIPT_NAME, then is restored”: drop the two expect_identical(req$...) lines after the call; rename to “…to SCRIPT_NAME”.
    • :101 “async endpoints return a promise of an httpResponse”: drop the final expect_identical(req$PATH_INFO, "/api/async").
    • :113 “the prefix stays stripped until an async filter has finished routing”: keep. It now asserts that plumber sees the stripped path inside an async filter, which is still worth pinning.
    • :41 “non-prefix paths fall through untouched”: keep unchanged. The fallback runs before any rewrite.
  2. Code: delete old_script, restore(), async, the on.exit, and the promises::finally(restore) link. The handler becomes: match prefix or fall back; rewrite SCRIPT_NAME/PATH_INFO; run guard; pr$call(req); convert sync, or then(rook_to_httpResponse) |> catch(mount_failure) for a promise; the outer tryCatch(error = mount_failure) stays.
  3. DECISIONS entry with the joinHandlers reasoning above, so the M1 entry’s “restored when the request finishes” is visibly superseded.

M10: Partials are checked once

Why. check_partial_refs() (R/page.R:161) errors at construction for any {{> name}} not in partials. render_whisker() (R/page.R:178) then also runs every render inside setwd() to an empty temp directory and promotes whisker’s “No partial” warning to an error. The only case the second adds is a tag after a {{=<% %>=}} delimiter change. setwd() per request in a server is a global side effect, and the construction check is the one that gives the better error anyway.

  1. Tests, test-page.R:
    • :143 “a partial the template uses but nobody supplied is an error at creation”: keep. This is the surviving rule.
    • :151 “a missing partial at render is an error, not a file lookup”: delete. It writes nav.mustache to disk to prove the render-time guard; that guard goes.
    • :115 “cache = TRUE renders once”: mocks render_whisker, so the function must keep its name and signature.
  2. Code: render_whisker() becomes whisker::whisker.render(template, data = data, partials = partials). Delete empty_dir() and in_dir().
  3. Docs: ?spigot_page Templates section says a missing partial “is an error (spigot does not look for whisker’s name.mustache files)”. Make it “is an error when the page is created”.
  4. DECISIONS entry: after a delimiter change, an unknown partial falls back to whisker’s default (a .mustache lookup in the working directory, else a warning and empty output). Accepted: the construction check catches every ordinary case.

M11: spigot.js in current JavaScript

Why. The file header says ES5 syntax, no build step. It also requires fetch, Promise, URL and AbortController. No browser has those and lacks class, arrow functions, const/let, template literals, spread or async/await. The ES5 rule buys nothing and costs the hand-built promise in request(), the Object.create(Error.prototype) constructor, withOption(), and the typeof X !== "undefined" guards in isRawBody().

The e2e tests are the spec and do not change: test-client.R:71-278, test-push.R:373-493, test-trigger.R, and the browser tests in test-page.R and test-examples.R. Run them before and after.

  1. Baseline: ES2017 (the year async/await shipped everywhere AbortController did). Say so in the header comment, replacing the ES5 sentence. Still no build step; still served as is.
  2. Keep the IIFE and "use strict". A top-level const in a classic script is a global lexical binding shared with the page’s own scripts, and the examples declare const $. The IIFE is what keeps spigot’s names private.
  3. Keep it a classic script, not type="module". A module is deferred and sees document.currentScript === null, which would break the data-prefix read at line 12 and the load-order guarantee that shiny.js runs first.
  4. SpigotError: class SpigotError extends Error with name, status, body set in the constructor. test-client.R:202 checks instanceof spigot.SpigotError, .status, .message, .body; instanceof Error must still hold.
  5. request(): an async function. Build init as now; wrap the body in Promise.race([timeout, run()]) where timeout rejects with the status-0 SpigotError after options.timeout ms and aborts the controller, and run() awaits spigot.ready, sets the session header last, fetches and reads the body, mapping a non-SpigotError rejection to the status-0 “network error” form. clearTimeout in a finally. The semantics tested at test-client.R:135 (waits for ready), :225 (timeout counts from the call, signal.aborted), :241 (network failure) and :250 (header cannot be overridden) stay.
  6. withOption() becomes { ...options, query } / { ...options, body } (only when the value is not undefined, as now).
  7. isRawBody(): drop the typeof guards; plain instanceof chain.
  8. Everything else (encodeQuery, apiUrl, readBody, listeners, dispatch, handlers, onFragmentClick) is a mechanical conversion to const/let, arrows and template literals. Do not change logic while converting.
  9. Docs: neither vignettes/client.Rmd nor ?spigot_dependency mentions ES5. client.Rmd:11 says “plain JavaScript with no build step”, which stays true. Only the header comment of spigot.js changes.
  10. DECISIONS entry: ES2017 baseline and why; classic script and IIFE kept, with the two reasons above.

M12: Help pages are reference, vignettes are narrative

Why. ?spigot_dependency documents the whole JavaScript API; vignettes/client.Rmd does it again. ?spigot_emit and ?spigot_trigger were written as the drafts of vignettes/reactivity.Rmd (DECISIONS, M4 and M6) and still read like it. Two copies to keep in sync on every behaviour change.

Rule for each page: keep the first paragraph (what it is, when to call it), every @param, @return, @examples, and any sentence that states a contract (shapes, ordering guarantees, what errors). Move or delete explanation (how it works internally, design rationale, alternatives) if the vignette already has it; if the vignette does not, move it there, do not delete it.

  1. Before editing, diff each page against its vignette section and list the sentences only the help page has. Those move to the vignette first.
    • ?spigot_dependency ↔︎ client.Rmd “Calling the API”, “Errors”, “The session”, “Events from R”, “Links on nested pages”.
    • ?spigot_emit ↔︎ reactivity.Rmd “Push” (the chat-room example is already there).
    • ?spigot_trigger ↔︎ reactivity.Rmd “The bridge”.
  2. ?spigot_dependency: the bulleted JS API list and the paths/bodies paragraph become one paragraph naming spigot.get(), spigot.post(), spigot.on() and SpigotError, then vignette("client", package = "spigot"). Keep the prefix param, the data-prefix mechanism (that is the contract), and the example.
  3. ?spigot_emit: keep the one-tab/all-tabs sentence, the spigot_json() shape sentence, and the “an event can reach the page before the HTTP response” sentence (contract). Delete the future worker paragraph and the “no replay” sentence; reactivity.Rmd:78-87 already has both. Keep the two examples.
  4. ?spigot_trigger: keep the first paragraph, the “value never leaves R, input is identical()” sentence (contract), the “fires every time, even with the same value” sentence (contract), and the namespacing sentence. reactivity.Rmd:90-123 (“The bridge”) already explains the id swap, the extra websocket trip, running after the endpoint returns, and every-trigger-fires. Delete those paragraphs from the page; only priority: "event" is named nowhere else, and it is an implementation detail, so it goes too.
  5. ?spigot_app: out of scope for this pass; its five sections are mostly contract. Revisit if M12 goes well.
  6. devtools::document(); rcmdcheck must show no Rd cross-reference warnings; pkgdown::build_site() locally and read the three pages and two articles once.

M13: Release 0.1.1

  1. NEWS.md: one entry. “Internal simplification; no change to behaviour. spigot.js now uses current JavaScript syntax (ES2017), same browser support. A {{> name}} partial missing from partials is caught when the page is created.” Mention the /reactlog 404 in one clause.
  2. DESCRIPTION version 0.1.1.
  3. Full suite with Chrome locally; push; all 4 CI cells green, including the shiny 1.11.0 cell (the ES2017 change has nothing to do with shiny, but the e2e tests there are the broadest browser check we have).
  4. pkgdown workflow green; site shows the trimmed pages.
  5. Tag v0.1.1.

4. Deliberately not in this pass

  • spigot_broadcast(except =) could be expressed with filter = and dropped (~20 lines with check_except() and root_session()). It is public API; removing it is a 0.2.0 question, not a cleanup.
  • run_example()’s three functions could collapse onto match.arg(). Harmless as is.
  • helper-proxy.R (85 lines, 3 tests) is the heaviest test infrastructure for the least verified payoff (DECISIONS, M2 and M3: real deployments unchecked). Keep until a real Shiny Server or Connect deployment either confirms or replaces it.
  • The looks_like_text() template-or-path heuristic, the later::later() static-path exclusion, the </head> split, by-reference spigot_trigger(), and the <base href> plus fragment-click handler all have recorded reasons and stay.

5. Next release: 0.2.0 — a Flask-shaped surface (M14–M17)

Design conversation 2026-10-21. spigot was written to give a Flask + Jinja development flow on a Shiny Server platform. 0.1.x has the pieces (pages, whisker templates, partials, a plumber API, www/) but not the shape: no blueprint, no template search path, no static dirs beyond www/, every file path relative to the working directory. 0.2.0 adds that shape additively: every new argument defaults to 0.1.1 behaviour, the three examples and apps/launch/ run unchanged until M17 rewrites one of them to show the new surface.

Target surface, so the milestones below have something to point at:

# app.R
spigot_app(
  pages      = list("/" = spigot_page("index.html")),
  api        = "api.R",
  blueprints = list("/cars" = cars, "/model" = model),   # objects from R/
  templates  = "templates",            # search path: dirs and/or files
  partials   = "templates/partials",   # a dir: one partial per file, keyed by stem
  static     = "static",               # served at /static; named list for several
  root       = "."                     # what the paths above resolve against
)

# R/cars.R
cars <- spigot_blueprint(
  pages     = list("/" = spigot_page("list.html"), "/model" = spigot_page("model.html")),
  api       = "api/cars.R",            # mounted at /api/cars
  templates = "templates/cars",        # searched before the app's
  partials  = "templates/cars/partials",
  static    = "static/cars"            # served at /cars/static
)

Decisions taken in the design conversation, to be entered in DECISIONS.md as each milestone lands (the “why” belongs there, not here):

  • Paths resolve against root at construction, and root defaults to the working directory then. In directory mode that is the app directory (DECISIONS, 2026-10-21 launch modes); in object mode it is whatever it is, as for templates today.
  • Static dirs are served by httpuv, not R. addResourcePath() takes one segment, but server$setStaticPath() takes any prefix, and mount_app() already calls it at start. Directory mode: set the paths in the existing on-start hook. Object mode: app$staticPaths, which runApp(<appobj>) honours (the “considered” option of the launch-modes decision, now with root to make it right).
  • No filename-only static references. src="cars.js" would need every static dir root-mounted, which Shiny owns in directory mode, so spigot would serve files from R after a page miss and file names would collide with page paths. Instead src="static/app.js" resolves at any depth via the <base href>, and a blueprint page gets {{static}} in its data ("cars/static") so its template needs no knowledge of its prefix. whisker has no lambdas (checked: a function as a section value renders empty), so a Flask url_for helper is not possible; a variable is.
  • A blueprint’s API mounts under the app prefix, /api/<name>/..., with plumber::pr_mount(). One guard, one prefix for spigot.js, check_pages_vs_prefix() unchanged; the client calls spigot.get("cars/fit"). Flask’s /cars/api/... was considered and rejected for those three reasons.
  • Template files are read when the app is built, not when spigot_page() is called, because a name can only be resolved once the page knows its blueprint and the app’s search path. Still before the app runs; the “can’t find” error keeps its text and gains the search path it tried.
  • www/ and R/ stay Shiny’s. static is in addition to www/, never a replacement. Blueprints live in R/ because Shiny loads it; spigot adds no loader.

Open, defaults chosen for this plan: dynamic segments (/cars/<id>) are not in 0.2.0; data = function(req) reads the query string, and converters are a 0.3.0 question.

Ground rules of §1 apply. Line references are to the 0.1.1 sources once M13 is tagged. Expectation count goes up in every milestone; note the number in each commit message.

M14: root and static

Why. Independent of templates and blueprints, and testable against the apps/launch/ fixture and test-launch.R already in place for the launch-modes decision. Lands the httpuv static-path mechanism that blueprints reuse.

  1. Test, test-launch.R: add static/extra.js to apps/launch/ and a static = argument to its app.R. Directory mode (all three existing launch tests) and object mode serve /static/extra.js with a JavaScript content type. www/app.js keeps its existing expectations in both modes (404 in object mode: unchanged).
  2. Test, new test-static.R (unit, no server): check_static() accepts a string (prefix /static), a named list (prefix /<name> each), rejects an unnamed list of two, a name with a slash, a name in reserved_prefixes, a dir that does not exist (error names root), and a prefix equal to or under the API prefix.
  3. Test, test-static.R: resolve_root() with root = "." returns the normalized working directory; with a relative root resolves it against the working directory; errors when the dir does not exist.
  4. Code, new R/static.R: check_static(), resolve_root(), static_paths() returning a named list of normalized dirs keyed by URL prefix.
  5. Code, R/mount.R: mount_app() gains static = list(). Directory mode: the existing on-start later::later() call also sets the static paths. Object mode: app$staticPaths is set from the same list. Both from one helper so the two modes cannot drift.
  6. Code, R/app.R: spigot_app(static = NULL, root = "."). NULL is 0.1.1 behaviour exactly. Help: a “Files” section replacing the www/ sentence in “Running the app”.
  7. Test, test-page.R: a page at /docs/intro whose template has <script src="static/a.js"> loads it (the <base href> already does this; the test pins that static and nested pages compose).

M15: template search path and partial dirs

Why. spigot_page("index.html") should mean “the template named index.html”, not “the file at ./index.html”, once the app says where templates are. Blueprints need the loader to exist before they can put their own dir in front of it.

  1. Test, new test-templates.R: template_loader(dirs, root) finds a.html in the second dir when the first lacks it; the first dir wins on a tie; a single file in templates = is found by basename; a name that is a path relative to root still resolves last (0.1.1 compatibility); the error for a miss lists the dirs tried.
  2. Test, test-templates.R: partials = "<dir>" yields one partial per file keyed by the filename without extension; a dir with nav.html and nav.mustache is an error (duplicate key); a named list is unchanged; a list may mix dirs and strings only at the top level (list(nav = "x.html"), not list("dir")).
  3. Test, test-page.R: spigot_page("missing.html") no longer errors at creation; spigot_app(pages = spigot_page("missing.html")) errors with the 0.1.1 message plus the search path. Move the existing “can’t find” expectations accordingly. Text templates (looks_like_text()) are untouched and still render at creation.
  4. Code, R/page.R: spigot_page() keeps the template string unresolved when it is a path; render is built by a new resolve_page(page, loader, partials) called from as_pages(). print.spigot_page() shows “unresolved” until then. The </head> and partial-reference checks (M10) move to resolve_page(), same messages.
  5. Code, new R/templates.R: template_loader(), read_partials_dir(), merge_partials(app, page) (page-level partials win over app-level).
  6. Code, R/app.R: spigot_app(templates = NULL, partials = NULL). NULL is 0.1.1 behaviour. templates = "templates" is not the default: a default that depends on whether a dir exists is the kind of guess the launch-modes decision warns about. The vignette shows the one-line opt-in.

M16: blueprints

Why. The point of the release. Built on M14 (per-blueprint static prefix) and M15 (per-blueprint loader and partials).

  1. Test, new test-blueprint.R (unit): spigot_blueprint() returns a spigot_blueprint with pages, api (a Plumber, from a file or router or NULL), templates, partials, static; rejects a page path that is not a page path, an api that is neither; print() lists pages and whether it has an API.
  2. Test, test-blueprint.R: register_blueprints(app_pages, blueprints, prefix) returns the merged page list with /cars + / = /cars, /cars + /model = /cars/model; a collision with an app page or another blueprint is an error naming both; a blueprint prefix under the API prefix is an error (reuse check_pages_vs_prefix()); / is not a valid blueprint prefix.
  3. Test, test-blueprint.R: a blueprint page’s data gains static = "cars/static" when the blueprint has static, and nothing otherwise; a function data gets it added to its result; a user key static wins (documented, not an error).
  4. Test, test-blueprint.R (server, helper-server.R): an app with one blueprint serves /cars, /cars/model, /cars/static/cars.js, and /api/cars/fit; the session guard applies to /api/cars/fit (401 without a token); the blueprint’s templates dir shadows the app’s for a same-named template; the blueprint’s partial nav shadows the app’s.
  5. Test, test-client.R: spigot.get("cars/fit") reaches the mounted router (one e2e case; the prefix handling in spigot.js is unchanged, this pins that).
  6. Code, new R/blueprint.R: spigot_blueprint(), print.spigot_blueprint(), register_blueprints(). API mounting: plumber::pr_mount(app_pr, "/<name>", bp_pr) where <name> is the blueprint prefix without its slash; spigot_api() builds the blueprint router so it gets spigot_json(). Static: each blueprint’s dir is added to the M14 list under <prefix>/static.
  7. Code, R/app.R: spigot_app(blueprints = NULL); as_pages() runs after register_blueprints(), so every existing path check applies to the merged list. Help: a “Blueprints” section; ?spigot_blueprint is reference only (M12 rule).

M17: example, vignette, release 0.2.0

  1. Rewrite inst/examples/site/ onto the new surface: templates/, static/, the /cars and /model pages as two blueprints in R/, www/ gone from it. The test-examples.R expectations for site change only in the URLs of its script files; the page content expectations stay. minimal and live are left on the 0.1.1 surface on purpose, so both ways are exercised.
  2. New vignette flask-flow.Rmd: the project layout, one blueprint, what root means under each launch mode. Narrative only (M12 rule); the help pages hold the argument details.
  3. NEWS.md 0.2.0: blueprints, template search path, partial dirs, static dirs, root; “template files are now read when the app is built”. No breaking change.
  4. DESCRIPTION 0.2.0; full suite with Chrome; 4 CI cells green; pkgdown green; tag v0.2.0.

Deliberately not in 0.2.0

  • Dynamic path segments and converters (/cars/<id>). Needs a routing change in page_router() and a decision on how matched values reach data; 0.3.0.
  • A url_for-style helper in templates. Not possible in whisker without lambdas; {{static}} and the <base href> cover the cases found so far.
  • Serving static files from R so a bare filename works. Rejected above.
  • A default templates = "templates". Rejected above; revisit if the one-line opt-in turns out to be what every app writes.
